[Question] If apple would lose their monopoly over iOS and its apps, how would it change the gaming on iOS devices?

That's a good question. I don't know if anything would change in terms of performance or increased cross-platform support. We'd probably see a surge in emulators and other content that isn't currently allowed. Maybe better peripheral support as well.

This is a question based off of a false premise. A company cannot have a monopoly over a singular product that they create, and that alone has nothing to do with gaming. iOS is a proprietary piece of software, meaning that the source code is not available or visible to anyone aside from apple. Saying that apple has a monopoly over iOS is like saying Adobe has a monopoly on photoshop, or Mozilla has a monopoly over firefox. A monopoly means dominance over a service or product market to the point of being capable of manipulate the market. That is not an applicable term in this instance since iOS is a single piece of software.

Gaming on iOS devices is... well... just that gaming on iOS devices. Apple is a proprietary company that caters to a different market. I'll assume you mean, "What is iOS was open source?" This would mean that the iOS platform would be free to change if others were willing to supply those changes. This would ultimately mean that iOS could become rather fractured, much like the linux and subsequently android platforms. These changes could lead to more "gaming" but that is left up to who would be maintaining the new flavors is iOS.

However, while that is a nice idea, Apple will not make the iOS platform open source unless that is beneficial to the company. It is very unlikely that apple will ever do such a thing. In my experience it is best to speak with your money rather than asking "Why can't my phone do these things?" after the fact. Also, this is a real bloodbath of a question to be honest. Maybe you should try learning about what "monopoly" is or "open source software" or even the history of apple and their approach to technology.

TL:DR, this question is kinda like asking "If we were to teach apple trees to start making sweeter apples, would the apples become oranges?"
